title: Finite drag impacts that cancel orbital work increase pericentre in an opposite-node Kepler model
abstract: We test whether finite drag impacts can evade a weak-impact constraint on a stalled orbital period. For two opposite disc crossings with exact intermediate Kepler motion, we prove that cancellation of nonzero orbital work increases squared angular momentum and pericentre. Gas speed is prograde, azimuthal and at or below the circular speed. Each impact forms a convex velocity mixture. The energy-gaining crossing must occur at the larger radius, for either order of work. An exact lower bound uses the exchanged energy and the actual crossing radii. In 40,000 synthetic inputs, 8,802 positive cancellation solutions pass the sign and identity checks, including impulse fractions up to 0.99990. Independent Cartesian orbit integration checks 20 cases. Repeated cancellation cannot keep orbital elements in a closed cycle in this model. For partial stripping at fixed penetration, stellar expansion or mass loss must offset the rising pericentre. This is a conditional proof, not new evidence that ASASSN-14ko has a stalled stellar orbit. Relativity between crossings, gas inflow, disc warps, mass exchange and emission delays are outside its scope. Original code, synthetic evidence and offline reproduction commands are included.

display.caption: Synthetic finite-impact cancellations obey the exact angular momentum lower bound and raise pericentre. No telescope measurements are plotted.

citations.reason: Extends its weak-impact proof to finite sequential impacts and both orders of orbital work.
